title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook: Integrations, Escalations, QBRs, and Known Issues
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates our standard process and templates for enterprise customer onboarding, integration checklists, escalation paths, common known issues and workarounds, the support process (SLAs and triage), and recurring health checks / QBR materials. It is intended for CSMs, TAMs, Solutions Engineers, and SREs who run or support enterprise deployments (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-value for enterprise customers, standardize incident escalation, and ensure operational readiness for production LLM inference workloads.
- Scope: Covers pre-sales handoff, onboarding week 0-12, integration handoff, production cutover checklist, escalation levels, known issues matrix, and QBR/health-check cadence. Not intended for internal development task tracking.

Owners and primary contacts:
- Document owner: Customer Success (owner_team).
- Playbook maintainers: Ava Martinez (Lead CSM), Jordan Kim (Solutions Engineering), Priya Shah (TAM).
- Emergency SRE on-call: See /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/oncall-rotation for current rota.

Overview: onboarding lifecycle (high level)
1) Pre-onboarding (Handoff)
   - Trigger: Contract signed and PO received.
   - Deliverables: Kickoff meeting scheduled, access matrix, legal/SEC/KMS requirements collected, initial architecture diagram.
   - Owner: CSM + Sales.

2) Week 0: Kickoff and scope
   - Agenda: Introductions, success metrics, SLAs (latency SLOs, uptime SLOs), data residency, compliance requirements, and integration plan.
   - Outputs: Project timeline (weeks 0-12), assigned TAM/SE, test dataset & prompt set, and access to staging account.

3) Weeks 1-4: Integration and validation
   - Integration checks (see "Integration checklist" section).
   - Validation tests: throughput baseline, 95th/99th p95/p99 latency tests, and cost estimate run with representative traffic.
   - Owner: Solutions Engineering + Customer Engineering.

4) Weeks 5-8: Performance tuning and security hardening
   - Actions: Adjust batching/timeout, select quantization profile, enable prefix caching as applicable, enable RBAC/KMS and audit logging.
   - Review: Security checklist and certificate rotation schedule.

5) Weeks 9-12: Cutover and QBR
   - Cutover plan: Canary rollout strategy, traffic ramp, fallback policy, and rollback plan.
   - QBR: Present performance, cost, reliability, and roadmap for next quarter.

Integration checklist (technical preflight)
- Account and access
  - Confirm: API keys for staging and prod, service account roles, VPC peering / private endpoints if Private deployment.
  - Keys/Secrets: KMS integration confirmed; rotation policy documented.
- Network & Security
  - Ports/whitelists: Ensure outbound to api.redwood.ai and regional dedicated endpoints.
  - TLS: TLS 1.2+ enforced, certs validated.
- Data flow & residency
  - Confirm log retention and PII handling, redact rules for prompts & outputs per contract.
- Model selection & operational profile
  - Target model version, preferred quantization profile, expected tokens/sec, typical prompt lengths.
- Observability & alerts
  - Enable metrics export (Prometheus or equivalent). Dashboards: latency by route, token cost by request, error-rate by model.
  - Alert thresholds: error-rate > 2% over 5m, p99 latency > target + 200ms for 10m.
- Performance validation
  - Run perf job: 30-minute soak at 2x expected peak with sampling of generation latencies and token counts.
- Cutover readiness
  - Rollout policy: Canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with 2-hour observation windows and automatic rollback criteria (see Cutover rollback criteria).

Support process and SLAs
- Support tiers:
  - Standard (self-serve + email): 24/7 ticketing, 72-hour P1 initial response for hosted customers.
  - Enterprise (CSM + TAM + priority support): 24/7 phone + ticket, 1-hour P1 initial response, 4-hour critical remediation SLA.
- Severity definitions (for triage):
  - P1 (Critical): Production outage impacting >50% of users or generation requests failing (total outage). Escalate immediately to on-call SRE and TAM.
  - P2 (High): Major degradation affecting a subset of users (e.g., p99 latency spikes, severely degraded throughput).
  - P3 (Medium): Functional issues without immediate business impact (API errors for specific routes).
  - P4 (Low): Feature requests, minor UI issues, or documentation gaps.
- Ticket lifecycle (steps):
  1) Intake: Customer opens ticket via portal/email/phone; CSM/TAM confirm severity and collect reproducible example.
  2) Triage: SE or Tier 2 assigns to SRE or product engineering with logs, request ids, and request samples.
  3) Mitigation: Triage owner attempts mitigation (config change, rollback to previous model, scale-up).
  4) Root cause analysis: Post-resolution, owner coordinates RCA and classification (build/regression/threshold/config).
  5) Postmortem or knowledge article: For P1/P2 incidents, create incident review and publish a knowledge base article if recurring.

Escalation playbook (contact matrix and steps)
- Level 0: CSM/TAM handles customer communication and tracks ticket.
- Level 1: Solutions Engineer triage for integration or SDK issues.
- Level 2: SRE on-call for infrastructure, runtime, or performance incidents.
- Level 3: Eng-serving-runtime engineering for kernel/kernel-scheduling, model-serving regressions.
- Level 4: Exec escalation (Director/VP) for contractual SLA breaches or multi-customer outages.

Escalation steps (for P1):
1) Immediately: Phone + ticket open with subject: [P1] <customer> <service impacted>.
2) Notify: On-call SRE and TAM via PagerDuty and Slack channel #inc-<customer-slug>.
3) Runbook execution: Follow incident runbook "Critical inference outage" (link: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/critical-inference-outage).
4) Customer comms cadence: initial acknowledgement within SLA window, follow-up every 30 minutes until mitigation.
5) Post-incident: Owner composes incident review and schedules a technical RCA with customer within 3 business days.

Known issues and workarounds (top recurring items)
- Symptom: Intermittent p99 latency spikes on long-prefix prompts
  - Likely cause: KV-cache thrashing when many distinct prefixes used in high concurrency.
  - Workaround: Enable prefix caching for frequent prompt families, increase cache size on Dedicated pools, or reduce concurrency per connection.
  - Owner: Eng-serving-runtime + Customer TAM.
- Symptom: Model downloads failing during private deployment install
  - Likely cause: Proxy certificate or firewall blocking outbound to model storage bucket.
  - Workaround: Whitelist model storage endpoints, validate proxy CA cert chain, retry with --resume flag.
  - Command example: curl -v --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/company-proxy-ca.pem https://models.redwood-internal.com/<model>.tgz
- Symptom: Unexpected higher per-token cost after quantization
  - Likely cause: Mismatch between model variant and kernel selection leading to tokenization differences or increased sampling repetitions.
  - Workaround: Re-run cost profiler with the selected quantization profile and revert to verified profile in the model catalog.

Knowledge base / artifact templates
- Integration runbook template (use during integration):
  - Overview
  - Preflight checks
  - Commands and sample requests (curl/SDK)
content_continued:
- Post-deploy validation checklist
- Incident postmortem template:
  - Summary, timeline, impact, root cause, remedial actions, and owners.

QBR and health-check materials
- QBR cadence and owners:
  - Quarterly business review (customer-facing): CSM + TAM + SE + SRE (on request).
  - Health-check (operational, recurring monthly): Solutions Engineer + SRE to review performance dashboards.
- QBR template (slides / doc sections):
  1) Executive summary: current status vs objectives
  2) Adoption & usage: token volume, active routes, top 10 prompts by volume
  3) Reliability: uptime, SLA compliance, incidents (last 90d)
  4) Performance & cost: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens per dollar, opportunities to optimize batching/quantization
  5) Roadmap & recommendations: model upgrades, dedicated capacity, cost-savings playbook
  6) Action items and owners with deadlines
- Health-check metrics to include:
  - Availability: 99.9% target for Enterprise Dedicated customers (SLA varies by contract).
  - Latency: p99 <= contract threshold (typical targets: 400-800ms depending on model family).
  - Error rate: <1% target for production routes.
  - Cost: tokens per USD month-over-month trend and outliers by route.

Cutover rollback criteria (example)
- Automatic rollback triggers during canary:
  - Error-rate rises > 1.5x baseline for 10m, or
  - p99 latency degrades > 25% from baseline for 10m, or
  - Token cost increases > 30% on canary traffic vs baseline.
- Manual rollback: Decision by TAM + SE after consulting SRE if safety nets triggered.

Post-onboarding wrap-up
- Deliverables within 7 business days of cutover:
  - Knowledge transfer session recording, runbooks, and production dashboard access.
  - Final QBR deck and optimization recommendations documented.
  - Signed acceptance checklist from customer.

Appendices
- Useful links:
  - Model catalog and verified profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding
  - Incident runbooks: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks
  - Observability dashboards: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts
- Template snippets (curl examples):
  - Example text generation request:
    curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'

Maintenance and review cadence
- This playbook is reviewed quarterly by Customer Success and Solutions Engineering. Any P1/P2 incident that reveals a process gap must result in an update within 5 business days.
